focus.label: Acquired perforating disorder
focus.why: node-2/3: follicular hyperkeratotic papules and hair changes; node-4 dialysis/CRF strongly linked to acquired perforating disorder; node-6 rules out other causes.

payload.query: Need skin biopsy histopathology with elastic fiber stain, dermoscopy, calcium/phosphate/PTH, dialysis adequacy, medication review, and hepatitis C/diabetes history (core to confirm acquired perforating disorder and exclude mimics). These are missing and critical.
payload.retrieval_output: Trichoscopy of the scalp revealed keratotic open follicular pores lacking hair shafts as well as hyperkeratosis and hyperpigmentation of the interfollicular epidermis. Histological examination of a scalp specimen revealed an enlarged follicular infundibulum, filled with keratin plugs, and follicular lichenoid tissue reactions in the infundibulum and isthmus. The interfollicular epidermis showed hyperkeratosis and partial vacuolar alteration along with numerous melanophages in the upper dermis. In the transverse section between the infundibulum and isthmus, a perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrate was seen with lichenoid tissue reactions and mild perifollicular fibrosis. A specimen from the trunk also revealed an enlarged follicular infundibulum with keratin plugs as well as dense lymphocytic infiltration with vacuolar alteration and dyskeratotic cells in the isthmus.

payload.report: Dialysis-dependent chronic renal failure patient has widespread brown follicular hyperkeratotic plaques/papules and scalp hair loss. Biopsy shows dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, perifollicular fibrosis, follicular plugging, lichenoid infiltrate, and vacuolar alteration. These findings strongly support acquired perforating disorder. Alternative diagnoses are unlikely given normal dioxin/sex hormones, no malignancy/collagen disease, and characteristic biopsy pattern. Despite no transepidermal elimination, this is the leading diagnosis.

frontier.label: Acquired perforating disorder
frontier.why: New expert analyses (pathologist and laboratory physician) describe biopsy findings of dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, perifollicular fibrosis, follicular plugging, lichenoid infiltrate, and vacuolar alteration, which support acquired perforating disorder, especially with dialysis-dependent chronic renal failure. However, no explicit transepidermal elimination is identified and metabolic labs (calcium/phosphate/PTH/glucose) are pending, so the diagnosis remains leading but unconfirmed; confidence adjusted from 0.85 to 0.88.
